Hi Samira — thanks for the questionnaire, and great questions. I answered the highlighted items below and attached our short evidence pack (hostedapi-data-map.pdf) plus the retention playbook excerpt you can share with legal. Summaries follow; see attachments for procedural detail and logs sample.

High level answers (hosted API):

1) Data residency / region pinning
- Customers may select a primary region at account creation. For Oaktree we can provision the tenancy in the US (us-west or us-east) and aim to keep all primary customer data and persisted artifacts within that region.
- Note: transient model inference requests may route within Redwood network for optimization, but persisted request logs, embeddings, and backups for a pinned tenancy remain in the chosen region.
- If you require strict geofencing for backups/snapshots we recommend Dedicated or Private deployments; we will document the boundaries for Hosted and provide controls to demonstrate residency.

2) Default retention windows
- Inference request payloads: ephemeral cache kept up to 24 hours by default for performance (can be disabled). No long-term storage of raw prompts unless you enable request logging.
- Request logs (if logging enabled): default 30 days; configurable up to 365 days under contract.
- Embeddings & derived artifacts: retained only when explicitly stored by the customer; retention follows the customer-configured TTL.
- Model KV caches: ephemeral and tied to runtime instance lifecycle; not part of persisted backups.
- Backups/snapshots: automated system backups retained for up to 90 days; per-account snapshot retention is listed in the playbook.

3) Tenant termination & erasure timeline
- Standard hosted workflow: initiation -> account data freeze -> wipe of active storage (S3/Block) within 7 business days -> snapshot/backups purge within 30 calendar days -> metadata and audit indices scrubbed within 90 calendar days.
- If you require accelerated erasure (e.g., contractual 14-day erase), we can commit to a shortened timeline under an SLA amendment and provide a signed operating procedure.

4) Evidence / audit artifacts
- Included in hostedapi-data-map.pdf: deletion runbook steps, example audit log (redacted), proof-of-wipe checklist, and sample KMS key rotation event.
- We can provide a time-stamped audit export for any erasure event (CSV) showing job ids, initiated_by, start/end times, and S3 object counts affected.

Next steps I recommend:
- Quick sync (15–20m) with our Security Ops and Rishi to walk through playbook and evidence.
- If Oaktree needs contractual region pinning for backups, we escalate to our Private/Dedicated team and produce an addendum.

Attachments: hostedapi-data-map.pdf, redwood-retention-playbook.pdf

Let me know what time works for you Monday or Tuesday and I’ll loop in Rishi (security ops lead) and Priyom (infrastructure).

Thanks,

Hi Samira — quick follow-up answers and attached redacted sample audit export as requested.

1) Cold/immutable copies
- We do not move hosted-service customer snapshots to a separate immutable jurisdictional cold archive by default. All backups/snapshots for a pinned hosted tenancy remain in the selected region and follow the same purge windows. If you require air-gapped immutable archives for compliance, we recommend Dedicated/Private deployments and a contract-level addendum.

2) Sample audit export
- Attached: erasure_audit_example_redacted.csv (CSV with columns: job_id, initiated_by, account_id, object_count, bytes_deleted, start_time, end_time, status). This is a redacted export suitable for review by Oaktree InfoSec.
